title: Hosted canary rollout: customer-visible timeline + audit activity panel
creator: Tessa Morgan
description:
Goal
Design the rollout details experience for Hosted canary rollouts, focusing on two tightly-related surfaces:
1) Rollout timeline: a clear step-by-step visualization of traffic split progression (1% → 5% → 25% → 50% → 100%), including state transitions (scheduled, running, soaking, paused, approval required, auto-stopped, rolled back, completed).
2) Activity panel: an audit-like, customer-visible history of actions and system events (who did what, when, and why), with enough detail to support change control and debugging without exposing internal-only data.

Why this matters
- During beta, customers repeatedly asked “what happened and why did it pause/rollback?” and support escalations had to correlate control plane events + SRE notes.
- GA scope includes customer-visible timeline + change history, plus alignment with audit log events (Security) for regulated customers.

Primary users
- ML/platform engineers running rollouts on production routes
- Admins/approvers (enterprise governance)
- On-call/SRE + support investigating issues with a customer

Entry points
- Console > Hosted Routes > Route Details > Rollouts tab > Rollout details page
- Console notification / banner linking to a rollout that paused / needs approval

Information architecture (proposed)
- Header: Rollout name, route, baseline model+version, canary model+version, current status badge, started by, start time, region scope summary.
- Primary tabs/sections:
  A) Timeline (default)
  B) Metrics (baseline vs canary) (DES-763)
  C) Activity (audit-like) (this ticket; may also appear as a right panel on Timeline)

Timeline design (step-centric)
- Timeline is a vertical, chronological list of “Step cards” with a compact progress indicator.
- Each step card includes:
  - Target split (e.g., Canary 5% / Baseline 95%) and step number
  - State (Scheduled / Running / Soaking / Completed / Paused / Failed / Rolled back)
  - Soak requirement and actual soak duration elapsed (e.g., “Min soak: 30m” + a timer)
  - Guardrails summary (max step, approvals enabled, auto-stop thresholds enabled)
  - Primary actions (contextual): Pause, Resume, Advance, Rollback (subject to permissions)
  - “View metrics for this step” deep link that pre-filters cohort comparison to the step window

State model (customer-visible wording)
- Draft: created but not started
- Running: traffic split is actively applied
- Soaking: split is stable and waiting on min soak time (or approval gate)
- Approval required: needs an approver to proceed to next step (explicit gate)
- Paused: user-initiated pause
- Auto-paused: system paused due to stop condition evaluation (pre-rollback) or metric evaluation failure (see edge cases)
- Rolled back: traffic returned to baseline (100% baseline)
- Completed: reached final target (typically 100% canary) and rollout marked complete

Copy guidance (align with DES-742 warnings)
- “Auto-paused” vs “Auto-stopped”: propose “Auto-paused” for temporary halts where customer can resume after review; reserve “Auto-rolled back” for destructive/automatic return-to-baseline.
- When displaying auto events, always include a reason line and a ‘Review stop condition’ link to thresholds.

Approval gates
- Timeline should show an “Approval checkpoint” row between steps when enabled.
- Approval checkpoint row includes:
  - Required role (e.g., Rollout approver)
  - “Requested by” + timestamp
  - Approver action (Approve step / Reject + rollback suggestion)
  - Optional comment field (stored in activity history)

Auto-stop / auto-rollback
- Timeline should surface the stop condition that triggered the system action:
  - Signal (5xx rate, timeouts, p95 latency regression)
  - Threshold and observed value (customer-facing; avoid internal metric names)
  - Evaluation window (e.g., “over last 10 minutes”)
  - Resulting action (Auto-paused / Auto-rolled back)
- Include a prominent “Rollback completed” banner when rollback occurs, with a ‘What changed’ link that summarizes traffic returning to baseline.

Activity panel (audit-like history)
- Activity is an append-only event feed with:
  - Timestamp (absolute + relative)
  - Actor (user name + org role, or “System”)
  - Action label (Created rollout, Started rollout, Advanced to step, Paused, Resumed, Approval requested, Approved, Auto-paused, Auto-rolled back, Rollback initiated, Rollback completed, Threshold updated)
  - Details snippet (diff-like: “Split: 95/5 → 75/25”, “Min soak: 30m → 60m”)
  - Optional reason/comment (user-entered; required for destructive actions per UX)
  - Links: “View metrics at this time”, “View config” (read-only JSON view), “View audit log event” (if tenant has Audit Logs feature)

Activity types to include (v1)
- Rollout lifecycle: create, start, complete, cancel
- Step changes: advance, revert to previous step (if supported), pause/resume
- Governance: approval requested, approved, rejected
- System: stop condition triggered, metric evaluation timed out, enforcement discrepancy detected (customer-friendly wording)
- Policy: action blocked by policy (should appear as UI toast, but also as an activity entry only if an action was attempted and denied)

Activity vs Audit Logs (important distinction)
- Activity panel is customer-visible and intended for debugging + operational transparency.
- Audit logs are security/compliance-grade and exported; activity panel should link to audit event IDs when available, but not imply it is the system-of-record.
- Proposed UI copy under Activity header: “Activity shows a history of rollout actions and system events. For compliance audit logs, see Audit Logs.” (Only show second sentence if feature enabled.)

Empty/error states
- If metrics are delayed: timeline still renders step transitions, but shows “Metrics pending” badges with last update time.
- If an event lacks an actor (legacy/backfill): show “Unknown actor” with tooltip.
- If user lacks permission: show timeline read-only; actions hidden; activity still visible.

Edge cases (from beta + SRE feedback)
- Metric evaluation timeout caused step to appear ‘stuck’: timeline should show a ‘Needs attention’ callout with suggested actions (retry evaluation / pause / rollback) and a “Last evaluation attempt” timestamp.
- Split mismatch by region (enforcement lag): show a warning banner “Traffic split not fully applied in all regions yet” with region-level status (collapsed by default). Avoid listing per-AZ.
- Streaming retries: do not show “double-counted” step transitions; activity is based on orchestrator events only.

Accessibility + internationalization
- Timeline must be navigable via keyboard; state indicated via both color and text.
- Use consistent badge shapes for status.
- Timestamps in user locale; show UTC on hover.

Deliverables
- Figma: rollout timeline step cards, approval checkpoint row, banners for auto events, and activity feed patterns
- Interaction spec: state transitions and action availability matrix by status + permission
- Copy deck for auto-pause/rollback reasons + destructive confirmations

Links
- Wizard flow: DES-742
- Metrics view: DES-763
- PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/hosted-canary-rollout-ga-prd.json
- Design spec: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/hosted-canary-rollout-workflow-design-spec.json
- Audit events spec: sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/audit-events-rollout-actions.json

Open questions
1) Do we show ‘auto-paused’ and ‘auto-rolled back’ as separate terminal statuses, or show status + last event? Current recommendation: status is the state; events explain the reason.
2) Should activity include policy/permission denials? Proposed: only when a user attempted an action (so it’s traceable), not for background policy evaluations.
3) Should approvals appear in both Timeline and Activity? Proposed: yes (Timeline shows current checkpoint; Activity is the record).
4) Do we allow adding a comment after an auto-pause to document decision-making? Proposed: add “Add note” action (non-audit) if easy; otherwise GA follow-up.

Acceptance criteria
- A customer can answer: What step are we on? What percent is canary? How long have we been soaking? Why are we paused? Who approved? When did rollback happen?
- Timeline reflects all major lifecycle transitions in a human-readable way.
- Activity entries map cleanly to audit events (ENG-9171) and include a stable event ID when available.
- Works in read-only mode for users without rollout permissions.
comments: 2025-02-21 (Tessa Morgan): Spinning this off from DES-742. Beta feedback: customers loved the wizard but had no confidence post-start; they want a ‘flight recorder’ view. Need tight alignment with audit events + orchestrator state machine.

2025-02-24 (Kenji Nakamura): Draft IA: Rollout details page with Timeline + Metrics + Activity. Question: do we make Activity a right-side panel on Timeline to reduce navigation? Testing both options in Figma.

2025-02-26 (Marissa Cole): +1 on activity being visible without audit-log entitlement, but language must avoid promising compliance-grade logs. Also want an approval checkpoint row that’s obvious (some customers missed approval gates in other workflows).

2025-02-28 (Marcus Lin): Please ensure we can display ‘Audit Event ID’ (or link) when Audit Logs are enabled. Also: actor should include auth principal type (user vs service account) if we support service accounts initiating rollouts.

2025-03-03 (Sean Gallagher): For auto-pause/rollback, we need reason text that’s actionable and non-alarming. Ex: “p95 latency exceeded threshold” + show window + observed values. Avoid internal metric names like ‘rw.http.server.latency.p95’.

2025-03-06 (Nora Ahmed): Implementation note: timeline needs a ‘system’ row type that isn’t a step. Orchestrator emits events that don’t correspond 1:1 to steps (e.g., evaluation retries). Design should support that without confusing customers.

2025-03-11 (Kenji Nakamura): Added ‘Needs attention’ banner for metric-eval timeout / stuck conditions. Banner includes: last evaluation attempt, suggested next actions, and link to runbook (internal only). Need to confirm what’s customer-facing.

2025-03-14 (Felix Schneider): For Activity diffs, avoid showing raw JSON in the feed; show compact diffs with a ‘View config’ drawer for full detail. This helps keep the feed readable and reduces risk of leaking internal fields.

2025-03-18 (Tessa Morgan): Copy review based on design Slack thread: prefer ‘Auto-paused’ (temporary) vs ‘Auto-rolled back’ (destructive). Add confirmation modal copy for manual rollback requiring a reason/comment (stored in Activity).

2025-03-21 (Kenji Nakamura): Marking In Review. Figma links shared in #design for review. Pending: finalize region-scope warning pattern (split mismatch) and the wording for ‘Unknown actor’/legacy events.
